title: Obstacle-Aware Length-Matching Routing for Any-Direction Traces in Printed Circuit Board
problem: Automatic length matching in PCB routing must adapt to any-direction traces while preserving original routing and handling obstacles. Traces must be assigned to non-overlapping regions and meandered within those regions to achieve target lengths.
motivation: Length matching is critical for maintaining signal integrity and timing requirements in high-speed PCB designs.
method: The approach works in two stages. First, it assigns each electrical trace to its own non-overlapping region on the circuit board. Then, it winds (meanders) each trace back and forth within its region to reach the exact target length needed while steering around physical obstacles. For pairs of traces that must stay perfectly synchronized (called differential pairs in high-speed electronics), it uses Multi-Scale Dynamic Time Warping—a technique that keeps both traces at the same length as they navigate the board together.
key_novelty: The core innovation is using Multi-Scale Dynamic Time Warping to keep paired electrical traces at exactly the same length as they both navigate obstacles and wind through available space on the board.
contributions: Two-stage routing framework separating region assignment from trace meandering optimization
Obstacle-aware detailed routing approach for space utilization and constraint satisfaction
Multi-Scale Dynamic Time Warping (MSDTW) technique for differential pair routing
Maintains original trace routing while achieving length matching under complex constraints
limitations: Abstract does not discuss specific quantitative metrics, experimental details, or performance comparisons with named baselines.
primary_theme: automated PCB routing with obstacle-aware length matching
